assets.name: nemacki-strelac
assets.prompt: Use case: historical-scene. Asset: production transparent PNG animation sprite sheet for an existing small 2D side-scrolling WW2 game. Image 1 is the exact German infantryman's identity/equipment reference; image 2 is the approved pixel-art animation style reference. Redraw the man from image 1, preserving his field cap (do not replace it with a helmet), gray-green uniform, dark boots, belt, compact long firearm silhouette, proportions and facing RIGHT. Match image 2's crisp pixel clusters, restrained olive/brown palette, dark readable outlines and small-game-scale readability. This sprite will appear about 56 pixels tall, so simplify detail purposefully rather than drawing a highly detailed illustration and shrinking it. Deliver exactly FOUR equally spaced columns and THREE equally spaced rows: twelve frames, no other objects or panels. Each cell is the same size and uses an identical ground baseline at 88% cell height and fixed foot anchor; every frame including the fallen body must fit entirely inside its own cell with transparent padding. Row 1, four frames: standing ready, a subtle breathing/weight-shift loop, feet stay planted. Row 2, four frames: raise/steady rifle, brief small warm muzzle flash with shoulder recoil, a tiny dissipating puff and recovery, return to ready. Row 3, four frames: non-graphic hit reaction, knees buckle/backward lean, controlled fall, fully fallen soldier resting on that same ground line. The death row progresses clearly; do not merely rotate the whole static sprite. Consistent identity, lighting, pixel density, camera and scale in all twelve frames. Strict side view, not isometric. True transparent alpha background throughout, including between frames: no black, white, checkerboard or scenery, no ground strip, no cast ground shadow, no gridlines, no captions or watermarks. Target sheet aspect 4:3 (1024x768), exact regular four-by-three grid. Preserve all source insignia only as tiny original details; add no new symbols.

append.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / game sprite-sheet extension.
Reference image: the EXISTING 512x384, four-column, three-row game-ready rifleman atlas. It defines the exact character identity, body proportions, pixel-art style, muted olive uniform, field cap, dark boots, small light skin areas, dark outlines, camera, facing RIGHT, sprite scale and foot placement.
Deliver ONLY THREE NEW animation rows for this same adult game character, not a repaint of the reference rows. Output a FOUR-column by THREE-row atlas, exactly 12 complete square cells, overall aspect 4:3, genuinely transparent alpha background. The result will be appended BELOW the reference, becoming absolute rows 3, 4, 5. No old poses/death row in this output.
Grid: every cell represents 128x128 game pixels; at that resolution the root is (64,120), ground contact at y=120, feet centered around x=60. Match the reference's FIRST-row character body height about 97 pixels and head about 18 pixels, relative to its 128-pixel cell. Keep camera, scale, fixed horizontal root and grounded supporting foot IDENTICAL in all 12 new frames. Leave empty transparent margins. No weapons or hands clipping top/right boundaries.
NEW TOP ROW = rest, four subtly different frames: stands upright and RELAXED, rifle slung over shoulder with muzzle pointing mostly UP or held down along his side, NEVER aimed at a target. The same relaxed rifle position in all rest/walk frames. Only subtle breathing and slight head turns/weight shifts; boots stay planted. Recognizably the same long compact firearm, cap, gray-green jacket/trousers, belt and equipment as the reference.
NEW MIDDLE ROW = walk, four-frame PATROL WALK CYCLE IN PLACE: same relaxed slung rifle, relaxed shoulders, no aiming. Four distinct readable phases of ordinary walking, alternating contact / passing / opposite contact / passing, opposite arm/leg movement, supporting boot consistently on the y=120 baseline, no whole-body horizontal travel. Same anatomical scale as rest and the reference, no running, crouching or jumping.
NEW BOTTOM ROW = fireUp, four poses: standing posture and SAME soldier as the reference fire row, but the barrel points diagonally FORWARD RIGHT AND UP, about 50 degrees ABOVE horizontal, held against the shoulder. Frame 1: clean steady aiming pose, NO flash and NO smoke; this is the held ready pose between shots. Frame 2: same elevated aim with tiny warm yellow-orange MUZZLE FLASH right at the barrel tip and small shoulder recoil. Frame 3: same elevated aim with small local gray smoke puff at the tip, no flame. Frame 4: return to frame-1 elevated aiming pose, no flash/smoke. The weapon's visible slender barrel itself must clearly point up-right (not a horizontal gun with a diagonal flash).
Visual style: reproduce the source's understated crisp small-scale outlined pixel art, limited olive/gray/brown palette, no smooth illustrated gradients, no 3D rendering, no extra microdetail. It must look like additional frames from THIS EXACT sprite artist.
Transparency and exclusions: true transparent alpha-zero canvas/gutters/corners, no checkerboard or dark background baked in, no ground line, ground shadow, scenery, captions, labels, cell lines, UI, extra people, symbols or added insignia. No injury, no falling and no blood. Every pose and its entire weapon/effect stays inside its OWN cell. Exactly 4x3 cells.

assets.name: nemacki-jurisnik

MIDDLE NEW ROW, walk (4 frames in-place calm patrol loop): same relaxed shoulder-slung rifle, no aiming. True transparent alpha-zero background, gutters and outer corners, no ground stripe, cast shadow, scenery, text, labels, gridlines, captions, watermark or added objects. All 12 complete figures fit within their own equal-size cells without contact or overlap. Exactly 4 columns x 3 rows.

assets.name: opel-blitz
assets.prompt: Use case: historical-scene. Create a production transparent pixel-art vehicle sprite sheet for a small 2D side-scrolling WW2 game. Image 1 is the exact Opel Blitz truck reference: preserve the LEFT-facing strict side profile, cab, open slatted cargo body with four tall vertical posts, two large visible road wheels, proportions and small original red-white door marking. Image 2 is the approved crisp pixel-art style: readable dark outlines, controlled olive/gray/brown colors and simple shaded pixel clusters. Do not turn the truck into a caricature, toy, 3D isometric object or modern vehicle. Design for an on-screen truck width near 205 pixels, with only details visible at that scale. Deliver exactly FOUR columns and TWO rows, eight complete frames on a strict evenly spaced grid; identical wide rectangular cells, identical truck scale and wheel ground baseline in all frames. Target a wide 4:1 atlas: each cell is twice as wide as high. Row 1, four idle frames: wheels do not turn, subtle engine vibration and a small gray exhaust puff starting from the same exhaust outlet beneath the cab, expanding and fading. Row 2, four rolling frames: wheel spokes/hubs progress through a full smooth looping rotation, body has at most a one-pixel suspension movement, small controlled exhaust puffs progress and dissipate. Vehicle remains fixed at the same horizontal anchor; it does not drive across the sheet. All eight frames show the SAME complete truck, including both wheels, bumper, posts and rear body, with generous transparent padding for the smoke; never clip, overlap or morph vehicle parts. Strict side-on camera. TRUE transparent alpha background, no grass line, road, scenery, ground shadow, backdrop haze, huge smoke, panels, grids or text outside the vehicle. No newly added symbols or insignia. Small exhaust only, no fire or damage.
